newsitem.title: UK: SocGen Asset Management makes key UK appointments.
newsitem.headline: SocGen Asset Management makes key UK appointments.

text.p: Societe Generale Asset Management said on Monday it had made three senior appointments at its recently established UK subsidiary.
It said Peter Seabrook, former UK chief investment officer at Fleming Investment Management, would join as senior fund manager with responsibility for building the UK equity team.

It also said Robert Guest of Johnson Fry Holdings had been appointed head of compliance and legal, and Graham Wethered head of administration. Wethered was assistant director of client service at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
SGAM in May appointed Nicola Horlick and John Richards joint managing directors of the UK operation.

SocGen Asset Management is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SocGen with 500 billion francs ($79.6 billion) under management and operations in ten countries. It has a 10 percent market share in asset management in France but a limited international presence.
Its stated objective is to strengthen its operation in Europe and the UK is a key element in this strategy.

Horlick resigned earlier this year from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, owned by Deutsche Bank AG, after being suspended for allegedly trying to take her team with her in a defection to Dutch financial services group ABN AMRO.

SocGen is a major player in fund management in its home country of France but has limited presence internationally, and is seen needing to set up a strong UK presence if it is to build a strong international business.
Richards and Horlick worked together at Mercury Asset Management, which they joined at the same time.
Richards had been with Mercury for 14 years, and Horlick moved to Morgan Grenfell in 1991. Richards was head of UK institutions and chairman of the UK institutional asset management committee at MAM.
